rationale: This is a mechanical additive merge of two already-tested archive signals (issuance volatility and issuance acceleration) against the identical che/lct leg, so it cannot separate "substitutes vs complements" cleanly and mostly re-tests information already in the archive rather than adding a distinct economic mechanism.

Recasting issuance as a bounded 0–5 episode count is a genuinely different, outlier-robust construct and the outlier-vs-slope diagnostic motivation is sound, but the 2% threshold is arbitrary, the count will be heavily tie-clustered (many firms at 0 or 5), and the underlying multi-year issuance leg is close to the well-documented composite share-issuance anomaly, so the novelty rests entirely on the liquidity conditioning that has now been reused in five archive signals.

target_name: Dividend smoothness as commitment under thin liquidity
rationale: The expression is internally inconsistent with the hypothesis: non-payers have dvc/at identically zero and therefore zero five-year volatility, so NEG(VOL(.)) assigns them the *highest* "rigid commitment" score, meaning the signal's extreme long/short legs are populated by firms with no dividend commitment at all rather than by the pre-committed payers the mechanism describes.

target_name: Dilution against cash-flow coverage of obligations
rationale: The denominator swap is honestly framed as a diagnostic on the surprising positive alpha of the oancf/che version and oancf/lct is an economically distinct coverage concept, but this is now the fourth "RANK(csho growth) minus RANK(some liquidity ratio)" cell tested, so it risks being scaling-space dredging rather than a new mechanism.

target_name: Paying out while raising equity under thin liquidity
rationale: The simultaneity of inflow and outflow is a genuinely new construct in this archive with a coherent round-tripping story and the MIN conjunction correctly implements "both, not either," though the large mass of zero-dividend firms tied at the bottom of the first rank means roughly half the cross-section collapses to the (already-tested) liquidity leg alone, which will dilute the interaction's contribution to the spread.

target_name: Equity and short-term claims expanding together
rationale: This is effectively a rediscovery of the joint share-issuance and asset/liability-growth anomalies (Pontiff–Woodgate, Cooper–Gulen–Schill) in additive form with no interaction or conditioning, and it is also a one-leg substitution into the existing archive signal SUMRANK(dvc/che, GROWTH(lct,1)), so it is both known and near-duplicative.
